turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, Doctor. Little Thabo is three, weight fourteen point two kilograms. Temperature thirty-six point eight, heart rate one hundred and twelve, breathing twenty-four. Oxygen sat is ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lovely, thanks Sister. Come in, sit. Howzit — what's been happening with him?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's the ear, Doctor. He's grabbing the right one, and at night he just screams. Shame, the whole house is finished.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sounds rough. Start wherever you like, I'm listening.

[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Since the weekend. Friday he was grumpy, nothing I could put my finger on. Saturday night and last night he woke crying, wouldn't settle in the cot — ag, he's in a bed now, sorry, not a cot.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Two nights of waking and crying. And the grabbing of the right ear, same stretch of time?
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, the grabbing started Saturday as well. He points at this side. I think it's the right, I'm pretty sure.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Before that, was he well, or was there a cold doing the rounds?

[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A cold, about a week — runny nose, and a cough that was worse when he lay down. The nose is drying and the cough is only a tickle now. Half his creche class is off, the teacher even WhatsApped the moms.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever in amongst that?
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No fever. I felt his forehead and his back, he wasn't hot. We don't own a thermometer, but I know my child.
[SEG0012] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, sorry, his gogo was at reception. She told me he was boiling hot last night, she could feel the heat off his body, and she wanted that written down.
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag no. My mother fusses, Sister. He was sweaty from the screaming, not feverish. I was awake with him, she was in the other room.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll hold both versions for now, we won't force them to match. Thabo, which ear is sore?
[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Red car.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): A red car, not an ear. That's okay, we'll park that question. Mom, is anything coming out of the ear?
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No discharge. No blood, no pus. And he has not vomited.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): How is the eating and drinking?
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Drinking is fine, water, some rooibos. Food is half-hearted — yoghurt, two spoons of pap, then the plate goes.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any diarrhoea?
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Stool is normal. What is worse is lying flat, he cries straight away. Upright on my shoulder, he dozes. I know you asked about the tummy.
[SEG0022] person_4 (PATIENT): Eina. Ear.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Eina, shame, man. Has the ear been a problem in the past?

[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not like this. Around age two the clinic did a hearing test, and the sister said it was borderline and to come repeat it, but we never went back. My sister got married that month and, ja, it slipped.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): So you were told borderline, and it wasn't repeated. I won't put a number in the file that nobody actually gave you. Any surgery, or other medical problems?
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No operations. Nothing else really, he's been a healthy child apart from the usual creche colds.

[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And — this is not Thabo's — his father has diabetes and he takes metformin, five hundred milligrams I think, twice daily. I fetched the repeats, every robot was red, that's why we're late.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Dad's metformin stays Dad's. For Thabo, has any medicine disagreed with him?

[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, amoxicillin, long ago — he got a rash, maybe, or it could have been strawberries that same week, I don't know, doctor. I can't tell you when, he was little. We stopped the bottle and we've just avoided it.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not sure of the year, not sure it was the antibiotic, not sure of the rash. Has he had a rash in the last few days, with this illness?
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I looked at his tummy and his arms this morning. Skin is clear.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): What pain medicine has he had?

[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Panado syrup, hundred and twenty milligrams in five mils. I was giving five mils. Well, actually, the label for his age says seven point five, and last night and this morning I gave seven point five. Forget the five.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Seven point five mils. How many times a day are you managing?
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Maybe three times? I'm not certain. Yesterday afternoon we skipped it, stuck in the bakkie after my sister's place. So not nicely on schedule.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any ibuprofen, or medicines that belong to someone else?
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No ibuprofen. My sister has biotin gummies, for her hair, not for children. She held one out to him and I said no ways. That's her supplement.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Glad you did. Thabo, is the ear worse when you lie down at night?
[SEG0039] person_4 (PATIENT): Big dog. Gogo dog.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ha, I asked about the ear and got the dog. No stress, my boy, Mom's already covered that. You don't have to answer.
[SEG0041] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's like this at the clinic, sorry. Also the parking is stressing me, but carry on, I'll risk the fine.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll keep moving. I'm just going to look in the ears and the throat, and listen to the chest. Cold metal for a second, Thabo.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right eardrum is red and bulging, and the left eardrum looks normal. Throat is mildly pink with no exudate, chest is clear with no wheeze. Neck is soft, no stiffness, and I don't see a rash on the skin.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So you think it's infected? Do we walk out with an antibiotic?

[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): It looks like a middle-ear infection on the right, coming after the cold. He's not toxic, and the temperature today is normal. My first thought was to start amoxicillin now and nip it.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not amoxicillin. Please. Even if I might be wrong about the rash, I don't want to chance it.

[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair, that changes it — I won't prescribe amoxicillin. Looking at him again, comfortable enough, drinking, temp normal, I'm not starting any antibiotic today. I was too quick.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Watch it, then?

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja. Watchful waiting. Panado seven point five mils of that one-twenty syrup, up to four times a day if he needs it for pain, not above that. Keep fluids going. Rather keep him home from creche tomorrow.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My mother is going to say I came home with nothing.

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): You've got a back-up. If the night crying and the ear pain are not settling in two days, come back. If before that he feels hot, gets drowsy, stops drinking, or the ear discharges, come the same day. We'll choose a medicine then that isn't amoxicillin.
[SEG0052] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You won't write a just-in-case script?

[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): No script today. I was going to, and then the possible rash plus how well he actually looks changed my mind. Time and pain relief first. If we treat later, we decide it in this room.
[SEG0054] person_1 (NURSE): I can hold a Thursday slot at the desk if you want it locked in.
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Don't lock it. Only if he's not better. Mom, pitch up on Thursday if he's still sore or still waking, and any earlier day if he worsens. Nothing to collect from pharmacy.
[SEG0056] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If he's still crying with the ear after two days, we come. If he's settled, we stay home. That I can explain to my mother.
[SEG0057] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's a perfectly good answer, Thabo. You were brave with the otoscope. Go get the red car.
[SEG0059] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sister, if my mother phones again about him being hot, his temp was normal with you, hey?
[SEG0060] person_1 (NURSE): I'll put the thirty-six point eight in the note so we can tell her. Drive safe.
[SEG0061] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cheerio. I hope tonight is kinder to all of you.

test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
